text:
Alex M.: Heads-up — launched kernel+driver canary in us-east-1 (kernel 6.4.2, nvidia 535.104.07) at 10:00 UTC. Noticed Xid spikes (31/45) on two cards and ECC corrected rate rising. Opening triage.
Priya K.: :eyes: can you paste dmesg + nvidia-smi?
Alex M.: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=12345 ...
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU crash dump
ECC corrected: +124 -> +260 in last 15m
``` 
Carlos R.: Drain suspect nodes? `kubectl drain node/gpu-canary-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 
Jamie L.: Could this be related to last week's BIOS microcode update? Telemetry showed PCIe retrain count climbing on these hosts.
Mike S.: Telemetry link: https://dash.internal/pcie?range=15m&node=gpu-canary-17 (looks like link retrain spikes at same times)
deploy-bot: Canary rollout event: kernel-6.4.2 deployed to canary-group-1 (20 nodes)
Priya K.: Freeze the canary please. Don't push more. Collect nv-hostdiag, dmesg, nvidia-smi -q and /var/log/messages from nodes 17 and 19.
Alex M.: Action items: 1) Pause canary rollout; 2) Drain node/gpu-canary-17 & 19; 3) Upload nvidia logs to /mnt/triage/1934560000/; 4) Run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and a 1-hour stress (gpu-burn + memtester)
Jamie L.: Quick experiments: boot one node with `pci=realloc iommu=pt` and another with `pcie_aspm=off` to see if retrains stop.
Carlos R.: Does anyone have the older kernel/driver combo artifact id we should roll back to? I remember 6.1.x + 535.73 was stable.
Mike S.: I'll run an overnight burn-in on the two suspect cards and increase ECC scrub frequency. Assigning myself.
Priya K.: I'll add a prompt in Optimize to correlate Xid -> powercap/polling events and set an alert for retrain > 5/min.
Alex M.: If link training correlates, plan: gate kernel build, test driver 535.98 with PCIe fix on single node, then canary rollback if negative.
deploy-bot: rollback: kernel-6.4.2 -> previous-stable completed for gpu-canary-17 (2026-03-18T10:12:00Z) :white_check_mark:
Mike S.: Confirming burn-in running; will report results in morning.
Alex M.: Thanks all — will update oncall and incidents if we see escalation. :thumbsup:
